clusters.reason: Both repair a personal notebook page while preserving readability on both sides. The detached-versus-torn wording and intervening work-surface and drying discussion do not materially change the requested repair constraint.
Both plan a board-game evening for a newcomer who wants to watch before joining. The required response preserves observation as a genuine option without assuming consent to play.
Both retain an owner's direct-return instruction for a borrowed item and prohibit leaving it at the event venue through unrelated planning. The stand has an additional Monday deadline.
Both revisit a displayed object's exclusion from sale after discussing its maker or display. One is a family keepsake; the other is a sample, so the reasons and supporting facts differ.

Each establishes two easily confused personal objects in different locations, inserts an unrelated exchange, then probes the mapping. The objects and locations change while the retrieval pattern stays fixed.
Both require an exact abbreviated public credit while excluding a supplied full name after intervening drafting. One uses an initial plus surname and the other initials only.
Each supplies a fact for private context, excludes it from public or recipient-facing copy, and retains it for appropriate private use. The excluded facts and audiences differ.

The common dialogue pattern protects a reveal from a particular audience while other scene or message work continues. Event surprises, gift knowledge, and story spoilers impose different audience and content boundaries.

An early exclusion is carried across intervening planning exchanges into a later activity or draft: no scoring, jokes, mirrors, fireworks, unavailable tools, cameras, sharp tools, or live cooking. Worker-a repeatedly specifies two intervening exchanges; the excluded actions remain substantively different.

A fictional entity's non-speaking or non-character status must survive scene development before an encounter or draft. Receptive language ability, an inability to speak, and a fixed backdrop are distinct constraints.

A group event permits listening, passing, declining a question, or attending without performing or playing; later participation planning must preserve the option. These are related consent boundaries rather than interchangeable activities.

Each tests whether an allowed action or contribution remains optional instead of becoming mandatory. The entities and scope differ: shoes, exchange contributions, trying a demonstration, donations, and an itinerary stop.

A volunteer agrees to one named task but has not agreed to a neighboring task; two unrelated planning exchanges precede later application. Setting up versus washing, weeding versus trimming, and explaining rules versus supervising children should retain separate task semantics.

These plans separate owner, current holder, loan or gift status, and sometimes container-versus-content ownership. The same slot-swapping risk warrants a common future split boundary, but their handoffs and ownership transitions differ.
A purchaser or booker is distinct from a collector, with later role questions or delegated pickup. The ticket case additionally separates reimbursement, attendance, and possession.

Each worker-b plan replaces an initial label or entity slot with a corrected value, discusses two other aspects, and must use the corrected value later. The corrected dimensions—game mode, time of day, relationship, subject, season, temperament, practice time, shape, and setting—are different.

Each corrects who performs which event or volunteer role, then retains the corrected assignment after two planning detours. Introducing versus performing, switching sorting materials, and assisting versus demonstrating have different role implications.

A specific episodic fact is stated, two unrelated topics intervene, and a final question asks for that fact. The requested facts cover causes, actions, timing, source beliefs, time-zone ownership, and object selection, so they should not be treated as identical answers.
A proposal or discussion must not be promoted to a decision. The later states differ: some remain undecided, while the club preference eventually becomes a confirmed future change.
Feedback is restricted to an identified dimension or target and must exclude another dimension. The final plan changes scope over time; the others retain a standing boundary.

coverage_note: Reviewed the supplied plan descriptions across root, worker-a, worker-b, and legacy310 for plan-level similarities. The clusters are a prioritized, non-exhaustive set of future split boundaries; all candidates remain train only. A shared boundary does not by itself warrant rejection or establish full-dialogue duplication.
limitations: Only openings and plan descriptions were supplied; generated dialogue, exact wording, and actual turn execution were not inspected.
Likely cosmetic judgments are provisional because detailed constraints and answer patterns may differ in generated dialogues.
Unlisted plans are not certified semantically independent, and these clusters do not constitute release acceptance or full-dialogue decontamination.
